name: Amethyst Thunderoak
reason: Source treasure plant 'Purple Thunder Bamboo' was renamed 'Amethyst Thunderoak' to fit the Western fantasy register (purple->amethyst, bamboo->oak).
description: A rare and coveted treasure plant that becomes the object of Zane's quest in the later arcs. In the source it grows only in a very special environment on Extreme Yin Mountain, and its sudden appearance drives martial artists to ruthless schemes to obtain it.

name: Raven
reason: The source epithet 'Black Crow' was localized to the equivalent dark-bird name 'Raven', keeping the ominous masked-antagonist flavor.
description: Leader of the Black Mountain Order, one of the fourth-grade sects contending at the Rising Dragon Arena arc. An old man who wears a black, expressionless mask, he appears alongside the other fourth-grade sect leaders Lady Darkmere and Tia (source: Black Crow, who stands with Madam Poison Blood and Ning Yudie) and demands answers from Zane.

name: Elder Julian
reason: The character's Chinese name Zhao Zheng was fully localized to the US-style name 'Julian', with the 'Elder' title kept to mark his rank alongside Elder Howard.
description: An elder present during Zane's Baptism by Laws arc (Eps 439-450), counterpart to Elder Howard (source: Zhao Zheng, a longtime elder beside Elder Wei and a recruiter for a rival palace). He grows jealous of Zane's talent, clashes with Elder Howard, and ultimately departs with Alan.

name: Alan
reason: The character's Chinese name Nian Yang was fully localized to the US-style name 'Alan Nolan'; the episodes use both 'Alan' and the full 'Alan Nolan'.
description: A powerful, arrogant vice leader (source: Nian Yang, second only to the leader of the Fire Dragon Palace) who arrives in Ep 447 to inspect and recruit the young man who survived the Baptism by Laws. Confident and dismissive, he watches the black-sphere trial with the city lord and Elder Howard before leaving with Elder Julian.

name: Rex
reason: A companion in the imperial-army arc given the short, rugged US name 'Rex'; his exact source counterpart among the squad members (e.g. Zhao Xuyong, Yang Tai, Cao Lei) could not be confirmed.
description: One of Zane's companions during the Emerald Task Force / imperial army arc (Eps 64-75), named at the Dragon's Keep tavern alongside Max and Leo under squad leader Shane. He speaks up to defend Zane against the soldier Troy's dishonorable challenge.

name: Seth
reason: The character's Chinese name Tian Yi was fully localized to the short, sharp US name 'Seth', fitting an arrogant arena challenger.
description: An arrogant challenger who leaps into the battle ring in Ep 80 after winning three consecutive matches and mocks the Misty Peak pledge Dustin as a 'butterball' (source: Tian Yi of Vulture Peak, defeated by the fat disciple Zhang Wuxian). His signature Sacred Lunge and Metal-Element-infused attacks all fail to land before he is beaten.

name: Nature Creature
reason: Since the source 'Xiantian' realm is localized as the 'Nature Level', a 'Xiantian lifeform' became a 'Nature Creature' for consistency.
description: Term for a being who has reached the Nature Level and transcended ordinary human limitations; Life Force at this stage pulses visibly. Perrin of House Lowell becomes one with House Warrick's backing, a feat previously achieved in the family only by Zane's father Milo.

name: Ruin Ring
reason: Source technique 'World Annihilation Ring' was condensed to the punchier 'Ruin Ring' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A devastating trump-card ring technique unleashed with precise hand gestures against Zane in the Ep 85 arena duel (source: Liu Cunshi's World Annihilation Ring, ch. 71); withstanding it was thought impossible.

name: Lesser Lotus Flower
reason: The Buddhist source term 'Hinayana Lotus Flower' was localized as 'Lesser Lotus Flower' (with the Mahayana form as the greater), avoiding untranslated Buddhist terminology.
description: The nine-petal lotus manifestation most cultivators gain upon reaching the Life-and-Death Realm; enduring each Lesser Celestial Tribulation activates another petal, and activating all nine is a mark of great accomplishment. Zane's own lotus proves to be the rarer, greater kind rather than the Lesser Lotus Flower.

name: Lotus Flower
reason: Source term 'lotus flower' was kept literally; it is the umbrella concept covering the Lesser (Hinayana) and greater (Mahayana) forms.
description: The faint lotus image that materializes over a cultivator's head upon activation at the Life-and-Death Realm during the Lesser Celestial Tribulation. In the source it is divided into Hinayana and Mahayana varieties; Zane manifests the greater form in Ep 1104.

name: Gossamer Pavilion
reason: Source organization 'Lingyan Pavilion' was renamed 'Gossamer Pavilion' for the Western fantasy register; its sister organization Spring Fragrance Pavilion became the Silverwood Pavilion.
description: An elite recruiting organization of The Alliance that takes in only the top prodigies, scouting talents like Zane at the Mist Palace alongside the Silverwood Pavilion. Each new member receives a Gossamer Token (source: Lingyan Token) granting free passage and aid throughout The Alliance's supreme worlds.

name: Gorman
reason: The character's Chinese name Gao Han was fully localized to the US-style name 'Gorman', a sturdy name fitting a prideful spear-wielding prodigy.
description: A Mist Palace warrior and former pride of his family who carries a Maple-Leaf Spear and trains in the Hall of Blades (source: Gao Han in the Sword Trial Hall). Humbled by the talent around him, he comes to test a new spear technique and instead discovers the thousands-of-miles-long crack Zane left across the simulated mountain.

name: Ascending Well
reason: Source term 'Ascension Well' was localized as 'Ascending Well', a near-literal rendering.
description: A device used by the sacred orders of the Upper World to pull in promising warriors from across the universe; Zane's arrival through one raises questions about his origins.

name: Oaken Pavilion
reason: Source location 'Ginkgo Pavilion' was renamed 'Oaken Pavilion', swapping the East Asian ginkgo tree for the Western oak.
description: A trade hub established in Auspice City by the Violetwood Sanctuary (source: Purple Bamboo Sacred Land), doing business with the local factions and staffed by Demon Night warriors. Zane crashes through its doors in Ep 1127.

name: Nyla
reason: The character's Chinese name Ling Lan was fully localized to the US-style name 'Nyla', an elegant name for a Demon Night woman.
description: A Demon Night woman at the Oaken Pavilion who reverently addresses the Queen as 'My Queen' and is commanded, with her subordinates, to swear an oath of allegiance before the statue (source: Ling Lan swearing the King's Oath before Xun). She complies under the threat of her secret reaching the Queen of Punishment.

name: Cody
reason: The character's Chinese name Hou Da was fully localized to the casual US name 'Cody', fitting the leader of a band of brothers.
description: The eldest and leader of a band of brothers exploring the underground depths with a Lantern Pearl (source: Hou Da, eldest of the seven Hou brothers in the Yin Luo Underground Palace). In Ep 1152 he vanishes into the darkness of the third level of the Endless Abyss.

name: Saint Thunder Meteor Hammer
reason: Source weapon 'Holy Lightning Chainhammer' (also rendered 'Holy Thunder Chain Hammer') was localized as 'Saint Thunder Meteor Hammer' for the Western fantasy register.
description: The devastating lightning hammer wielded by the Queen of Punishment together with her brilliant blue Saint Sky Armor; charged with Faith Energy, it erupts in storms of lightning with a single swing.

name: Tanya
reason: The source character's epithet-name 'Scissors' was replaced with the natural female name 'Tanya', while her saber kept its one-word source name 'Slash'.
description: A female Demon Night (Fiend Night Clan) warrior who, with her male partner Maverick (source: Serene Dream), hunts Zane and his keep after the Wheel of Reincarnation battle. She wields a machete named Slash whose swing erupts in blinding, star-like light, yet Zane repeatedly evades her blade.

name: Armond
reason: The source title-name 'Empyrean Ling Huo' ('spirit fire') was localized to the strong US-style name 'Armond'.
description: An Empyrean-level powerhouse whose dragon-fire is mighty enough to incinerate a star, yet even his flames cannot crack the mystery-laden keep sheltering Zane (source: Empyrean Ling Huo burning the mini immortal mansion). He concedes that they can do nothing to Zane while he remains inside.

name: Water Law
reason: Source term 'Law of Water' / 'Water Law' was kept nearly literally for the adaptation's system of elemental Laws.
description: One of the elemental Laws of the cultivation system that warriors comprehend and specialize in, manifesting as shimmering waves of water; specialists in it fight cautiously from range.

name: Golden Celestial Paragon
reason: Source title 'Gold Demi-Immortal' (earned in the Talent Stele) was localized as 'Golden Celestial Paragon' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A prestigious title granted by the Talent Tablet (source: Talent Stele) to supremely gifted warriors, historically earned by an incredibly powerful World Lord. Zane's recognition with the title shocks the continent, and even Max's group struggles to believe it.

name: World Lords and Supreme Lords
reason: Compound plural phrase joining two rank titles ('World Lord', 'Supreme Lord') that are each covered by their own singular entities; not an entity itself.

name: Low Grade-One Divine Weapon
reason: The source's divine weapon grading ('first grade divine weapon', with low/secondary sub-grades) was rendered as 'Low Grade-One Divine Weapon' in the adaptation's weapon-tier system.
description: The lower tier of Grade-One Divine Weapons in the Upper World's weapon grading, normally reserved for World Lords and Supreme Lords and far beyond what ordinary warriors can obtain. Fenton's and Thane's weapons were of this grade, and Zane crushing one with his bare hands stuns onlookers.

name: Nigel
reason: The character's Chinese name Xuanyuan Chenfeng was fully localized to the US-style name 'Nigel'.
description: The former number-one prodigy on the Illusion Battlefield rankings (source: Xuanyuan Chenfeng of Gods Without Thought) who mysteriously plummeted from first to fortieth-thousandth place, implying he was killed once and lost half his points. He soon begins climbing the rankings again.

name: Cloud-Chaser Skill
reason: Source technique 'Chasing Cloud Movement Technique' was condensed to 'Cloud-Chaser Skill' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A wind-based movement technique (source: a Wind Escape Technique tied to the Law of Wind) that Zane masters with uncanny speed, grasping seventy percent of it in minutes. He channels Vitality into his legs to launch it, twisting clear of otherwise unavoidable strikes.

name: Apeiron Tower
reason: Source faction 'Indefinite Tower' was renamed 'Apeiron Tower', using the Greek 'apeiron' (boundless/indefinite) to keep the meaning in a Western register.
description: A powerful tower-faction that looms over the surrounding powers, home to disciples of Elder Apeiron (source: Indefinite Old Man of the Indefinite Tower). Cora (source: Xi Youqin) trains there as his direct apprentice, and the tower erupts in cheers at her Vanguard One Hundred ranking.

name: Formless Sword
reason: Source technique 'Formless', the sword art Luo Zheng created himself, was localized as 'Formless Sword' to clarify it is a sword technique.
description: Zane's self-created signature sword technique: not truly without form, but a single simple move containing the potential for a thousand others, making opponents' counters irrelevant. He uses it across hundreds of episodes to dismantle foes like Maddox and Logan.

name: Space Law
reason: Source term 'Law of Space' / 'Space Law' was kept nearly literally for the adaptation's system of Laws.
description: One of the higher Laws of the cultivation system, notoriously difficult to cultivate though still easier than the Time Law; mastery enables spatial techniques such as spatial blades and travel.

name: Palace Master
reason: Source title 'Palace Master' was kept literally as the institutional title for the head of a palace.
description: The institutional title for the head of a palace such as the Mist Palace, where Yolande holds the position against rivals scheming to force her out. The weapons of former Palace Masters are treated as near-sacrosanct relics.

name: Gareth
reason: The character's Chinese name Tu Jianbai was fully localized to the US-style name 'Gareth'; his sect, the Dark Moon Mansion, became the Mysterious Luna Hall.
description: A Soul Realm warrior of the Mysterious Luna Hall (source: Tu Jianbai of the Dark Moon Mansion) at the Dragon Soar Arena in Eps 451-452. He is confronted and blocked by Dominic, and left frozen in cold sweat by Zane's display of power.

name: Third-Grade House
reason: Source term 'third-grade family' was rendered 'Third-Grade House' in line with the show's 'Legacy House(s)' (not Families) naming policy.
description: A rank in the hierarchy of noble houses, well below the great houses; in Cloudhaven, Zane openly scorns the idea that the great houses would rally behind a mere Third-Grade House.
